extraction.Name: Mrs. Virgie Hudspeth, formerly Virgie Goings
extraction.Refused/Protested: called at the Agents Office, living at the Agency at that time, after hearing that patents were there and ready for delivery, and that she received the patent to the land allotted her
extraction.Sold/Mortgaged: sold the same two or three years after getting the patent, deponent does not know the exact date
extraction.Tax burden forced sale/Mortgage: she could not raise the money to pay the taxes during the time she owned the land, so sold the same; after getting the patent deponent states that she learned that if the taxes were not paid, she would lose this land; with that information at hand, deponent thought it was necessary to sell this land in order to save it
extraction.Occupation/Income: works when she can get employment by the day
extraction.NOTES: Deponent states she was not defrauded of her land but sold the same very cheap, and not near what it was actually worth; she had to leave the Government Service on account of ill health; received a payment of $10.00 in the fall of 1928 and no further aid from Government, State or County since her patent in fee was issued; she has no land at the present time, no home, and lives with some relatives at the U.S. Indian School at Rapid City, South Dakota; she is a widow; Pennington County, South Dakota; document subscribed and sworn before Notary Public Chas. B. Hunt on May 20, 1929; commission expires Sept. 6, 1931 | TASK 3 BULK TRIBE INFERENCE 2026-04-29: Tribe field set to 'Pine Ridge' based on directory provenance (record is filed in pine_ridge_*/extractions/, which corresponds to the NARA RG 75 Pine Ridge Vol 1, Vol 2, and Vol 3 bound volumes of Circular 2464 responses). 67 such records were originally 'not stated'; 6 received BLM-confirmed substantive patches in the same transaction; the remaining 61 (this record's batch) are inferred from directory and geographic/naming evidence.
